reader_summary.headline: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6 and Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6 and Z podcast. This episode is a podcast all about podcasting. Really, it's all about audio, and reruns an episode from last year that I'm resurfacing here as the podcasting and audio ecosystem continues evolving.

key_points.text: The conversation featured Nick Kwa, who writes a hot pod newsletter and column in New York Magazine's Vulture site.
key_points.evidence_quote: The conversation featured Nick Kwa, who writes a hot pod newsletter and column in New York Magazine's Vulture site, and A6 and Z general partner Connie Chan, who covers consumer as well as discussing audio trends from China in this episode.

key_points.text: Both of them joined me for a hallway style jam and pulse check on the podcasting industry in early 2019.
key_points.evidence_quote: Both of them joined me for a hallway style jam and pulse check on the podcasting industry in early 2019.

key_points.text: We covered everything from discovery, monetization, platforms, analytics, and more, including impacts on creators.

key_points.text: We touched briefly on the future of radio and went deep through lightning rounds on what happens when content and entertainment is created natively for audio..

thesis: The episode discusses the evolving definition of podcasting, noting a tension between its historical roots in RSS feeds and blogging versus its current perception as the future of radio. The speakers argue that while the technical definition relies on RSS, the cultural definition is shifting toward spoken word content that may blur with audiobooks, while explicitly distinguishing podcasting from music.
